text:
maria (sec-eng): Heads up — planning an RBAC tweak to the on‑prem control plane tonight (23:00 UTC). While validating in staging I saw repeated KMS decrypt failures and a weird pattern where a long‑lived serviceaccount token is being reused across namespaces. Could be an attacker or misconfig. Need quick triage before rollout.

sam (infra): Can you paste the log snippet?

maria (sec-eng): Sure, from staging audit-collector: 
```
2024-12-03T21:07:13Z audit: method=kms.Decrypt result=AccessDenied key=projects/internal/loc/keys/priv-deploy-key principal=system:serviceaccount:deploy:build-agent resource=secrets/credentials
2024-12-03T21:07:13Z auth: token_used=sa-token-abc123 reused_across_ns=true
```

lee (platform): :eyes: That principal shouldn't have Decrypt on that key. I thought the infra SA only had kms:Decrypt via a short‑lived role binding?

jen (ops): Reusing SA tokens across namespaces is a misconfig — we had a similar flub in sandbox earlier. Are we seeing serviceAccountIssuer or tokenAudience misconfig?

maria (sec-eng): staging cluster has boundServiceAccountTokenVolume: false on older nodepool; token TTLs were long. Looks like a workload picked up the token and used it to call KMS through a proxy.

audit-bot: Automated alert: HIGH - KMS access denied spikes (staging). Investigating correlated auth failures. Rule ID: kms-escalation-2124 :warning:

devon (ml-infra): Short term mitigation: 1) rotate the key policy to remove the infra SA, 2) revoke long‑lived tokens (if possible), 3) enable audience‑bound token validation on the control plane. We should also add an allowlist for KMS callers in the key's IAM condition based on workload identity.

lee (platform): Agreed. Steps I can take immediately: patch netpol to block egress from build namespace to KMS endpoint except via ksm-proxy svc, and apply a temporary deny on the suspect SA. Patch command I ran in staging: 
```bash
kubectl annotate sa build-agent redwood/security-revoked=true -n deploy
kubectl patch cm netpol-egress -n deploy --patch '{"data":{"deny_all":"true"}}'
```

jen (ops): I'll push a SIEM rule to alert on repeated AccessDenied on kms.Decrypt plus token reuse patterns. Also queue an off‑hour pager if it occurs in prod.

olivia (security lead): Quick checklist: 
- Stop rollouts to prod until we validate root cause
- Rotate KMS key or at least remove principal bindings short‑term
- Force token TTL shrink on the older nodepool or cordon nodes to force reissue
- Start incident call if we confirm any prod artifacts
I'll take ownership of the incident if it hits prod.

maria (sec-eng): I'm going to run an isolation canary in staging at 22:10 UTC: apply netpol egress deny, revoke SA tokens, validate that no legitimate jobs break. If green I'll block the rollout and we can schedule a maintenance window. Tagging @oncall.

devon (ml-infra): Detection rules to add (short list): 
- alert if same SA token used from >=2 namespaces within 5m
- alert if kms.Decrypt AccessDenied spikes >10/min from unique principals
- alert if KMS calls originate from non‑proxy ips

lee (platform): Also recommend updating KMS IAM to use Conditions with request.auth.principal (or workload identity attributes) and tight time windows. Example IAM condition: `request.time < timestamp("2024-12-04T02:00:00Z") && resource.name.startsWith("projects/internal/loc/keys/priv-deploy-key")` (we'll refine).

jen (ops): For on‑prem private: check the Bastion egress ACLs — don't allow direct 443 to cloud kms from nodes unless through the proxy. I'll push a rule to iptables on jumpboxes if we need immediate enforcement.

maria (sec-eng): We've also got a vuln triage note: CVE‑XXXX‑2024 affects kubelet token projection in older node images; might explain token reuse. I'm assigning a sweep: upgrade node images and enable TokenRequest webhook.

olivia (security lead): Good call. I'll add this to the incident runbook and notify compliance (audit trail needed). Please ensure audit logs are forwarded to retention bucket and we snapshot the staging logs before any rotation. Link to runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/priv-deploy-incident (internal).

sam (infra): If we rotate the key, coordinate with Dedicated and Hosted teams — they might be using the same key for test harnesses. I'll run a dependency check script: `./scripts/kms-dep-check --key priv-deploy-key` and post results.

maria (sec-eng): Action items and owners: 
- lee: apply netpol egress deny in staging (22:10 UTC) — in progress
- jen: SIEM rule + Bastion ACLs — queued
- devon: detection alerts + token revoke helper — WIP
- sam: dependency check on KMS usage across infra — WIP
- olivia: incident runbook + compliance notification — prepping

olivia (security lead): If we see any signs of exfil or lateral movement, escalate to full incident and call infra oncall. Otherwise, we can treat this as high‑risk config + vuln remediation.

maria (sec-eng): Updating here after staging canary: netpol applied, SA annotated, token revoke triggered. Staging jobs: 1 failing job (integration test harness) — investigating. No further kms.Decrypt AccessDenied spikes after mitigation.

jen (ops): SIEM shows alerts suppressed after 22:25 UTC. Paging threshold still set for prod.

lee (platform): Dependency check returned two non‑critical test harnesses using the key; both are in test projects — sam will coordinate rotation window.

sam (infra): Confirmed — will schedule key rotation 2024-12-04 03:00 UTC with rollback plan.

maria (sec-eng): OK — postponing tonight's rollout. We'll reconvene morning to finalize RBAC changes (remove long‑lived SA binds, enforce token audience, tighten KMS IAM conditions). Great triage team — :thumbsup:

olivia (security lead): Documenting timeline and lessons learned for postmortem. Please capture commands and timestamps in the runbook section.

maria (sec-eng): Will do — adding the staging log snapshot and the netpol patch diff to the runbook now.

audit-bot: Incident status updated: triage -> contained (staging). Next step: verify prod controls.

devon (ml-infra): I'll follow up with a short playbook snippet to rotate service credentials to ephemeral tokens for critical workloads.

maria (sec-eng): Thanks all. If anyone notices related alerts, ping this thread and @olivia.

lee (platform): noted.

jen (ops): thanks, closing action items for tonight unless something pops up. :zzz:

olivia (security lead): Nicely handled, team. We'll run a tabletop on Monday to validate the detection coverage.
